stem: A client uses supplemental oxygen at home. Which instruction is most important for reducing fire risk?

options.A: Keep home oxygen away from smoking, open flames, sparks, and heat sources because oxygen makes fire burn hotter and faster.
options.B: Permit smoking after the cannula is removed for several minutes because oxygen no longer contributes to fire risk once the device is off the face.
options.C: Place the oxygen concentrator near the cooking area so the client can monitor it while using a gas stove or other open-flame appliance.
options.D: Use petroleum-based products around oxygen tubing because they decrease friction and therefore lower the chance of ignition near the equipment.

rationale: Veterans Health Library home-oxygen guidance states that oxygen makes fire burn hotter and faster and instructs clients to keep oxygen away from heat and open flames, not to smoke or allow smoking nearby, and not to use oxygen while cooking. Separate VA oxygen-safety guidance also advises against petroleum jelly and oil-based products because they are flammable. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Reduce home-oxygen fire risk by keeping oxygen away from smoking, open flames, sparks, and heat and by avoiding flammable petroleum/oil-based products near oxygen equipment.

source_original.stem: A client uses supplemental oxygen at home. Which instruction is most important for reducing fire risk?

options.A: Keep home oxygen away from smoking, flames, sparks, and heat sources because an oxygen-enriched environment makes combustible materials ignite and burn more readily.
options.B: Permit smoking after the cannula is removed for several minutes because oxygen no longer contributes to fire risk once the device is off the face.
options.C: Place the oxygen concentrator near the cooking area so the client can monitor it while using a gas stove or other open-flame appliance.
options.D: Use petroleum-based products around oxygen tubing because they decrease friction and therefore lower the chance of ignition near the equipment.

source_original.rationale: Oxygen supports combustion and increases fire intensity. Home oxygen safety guidance requires avoiding smoking, open flames, sparks and heat sources.
source_original.source_detail: Safety tips for using oxygen therapy at home. VA patient education; last annual review 2024-10-01; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: infection prevention, biohazard handling, security plans, equipment safety and workplace safety. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the home-oxygen fire-safety construct and key A, tightened the wording to VA's exact 'fire burn hotter and faster' teaching, and added current VA confirmation that petroleum/oil-based products are flammable.

audit_findings.exact_locator: Understanding Oxygen Therapy > Safety tips; Using Oxygen Safely > Oxygen don'ts
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses directly supported fire-risk instructions and avoids an unnecessary mechanistic overstatement about ignition thresholds.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; smoking near home oxygen remains unsafe even if the cannula is briefly removed.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect; oxygen should not be used near cooking/open-flame hazards.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect; petroleum/oil-based products are flammable and specifically discouraged.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A gives the recommended overarching fire-prevention instruction.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are home-oxygen practices; A is determined by safety guidance rather than stylistic cues.
